title: Colimits of commutative algebras over a commutative ring exist
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $\mathcal C_R$ the category of commutative $R$-algebras (commutative rings $A$ with a ring homomorphism $R\to A$; morphisms are ring homomorphisms commuting with the structure maps). Then every diagram $D:I\to\mathcal C_R$ indexed by a small category $I$ (in particular every directed system $(A_i,\varphi_{i'i})_{i\le i'}$ over a directed set $I$) has a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] in $\mathcal C_R$. For $R=\mathbf Z$ this says that every small diagram of commutative rings has a colimit.

source.place: Algebra, Section 07N7 (section-colimits), Lemma 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit: the directed colimit of modules as the disjoint union modulo the relation, with sum and scalar multiplication defined at a common later index; the ring structure is defined in the same way, the product of the classes of $a\in A_i$, $a'\in A_{i'}$ being the class of $\varphi_{ji}(a)\varphi_{ji'}(a')$ for $j\ge i,i'$, and the structure map $R\to A$ is $r\mapsto$ class of $\sigma_i(r)$); general small diagrams: Categories, Lemma 002P (lemma-colimits-coproducts-coequalizers) with coproducts the tensor products over $R$
